Extract a signal using standard deviation

Source: R/extract_signal_standard_deviation.R
extract_signal_standard_deviation.Rd

Extract signal from a wavelet spectra in the depth domain using a the standard deviation of the omega (number of cycles) as boundaries. The uncertainty is based on the Gabor uncertainty principle applied to the continuous wavelet transform using a Morlet wavelet. The calculated uncertainty is the underlying analytical uncertainty which is the result of applying the Gabor uncertainty principle to the continuous wavelet transform using a Morlet wavelet.

Usage

extract_signal_standard_deviation(
  wavelet = NULL,
  tracked_cycle_curve = NULL,
  multi = 1,
  extract_cycle = NULL,
  tracked_cycle_period = NULL,
  add_mean = TRUE,
  tune = FALSE,
  genplot_uncertainty_wt = FALSE,
  genplot_extracted = FALSE,
  keep_editable = FALSE,
  palette_name = "viridis",
  color_brewer = "viridis",
  colour_brewer = NULL
)

Arguments

wavelet

Wavelet object (list) created with analyse_wavelet; the signal is reconstructed from its coefficients and its number of cycles omega_nr sets the Gabor (Morlet) uncertainty. Required (Default=NULL).

tracked_cycle_curve

Tracked period of the cycle along the record (matrix or data frame: depth/time in column 1, period in column 2, in the depth/time unit of the wavelet), e.g. the output of track_period_wavelet completed with completed_series. Rows with NA are dropped and the curve is linearly interpolated (and extrapolated) to the depth/time axis of the wavelet. Required (Default=NULL).

multi

Multiple of the standard deviation of the analytical frequency uncertainty of the Morlet wavelet that sets the band boundaries, 1 / (f0 -/+ multi * sd) around the frequency f0 of the (rescaled) tracked period (numeric, > 0); larger values give a wider band. Default=1.

extract_cycle

Duration of the cycle to extract (numeric, > 0), in the same unit as tracked_cycle_period; use the same value to extract the tracked cycle itself. The tracked curve is multiplied by extract_cycle / tracked_cycle_period. Required (Default=NULL).

tracked_cycle_period

Duration in time of the tracked cycle, e.g. 405 (kyr) for the long eccentricity cycle (numeric, > 0), in the same unit as extract_cycle; also used for the tuning when tune=TRUE. Required (Default=NULL).

add_mean

Add the mean of the original data series to the extracted cycle (logical, TRUE or FALSE); FALSE returns it centred on zero. Default=TRUE.

tune

Convert the extracted cycle (and the plots) from the depth to the time domain with curve2tune, using tracked_cycle_curve and tracked_cycle_period (logical, TRUE or FALSE). Default=FALSE.

genplot_uncertainty_wt

Plot the wavelet scalogram (with plot_wavelet) with the tracked curve (black) and the upper (red) and lower (blue) boundaries set by multi times the standard deviation of the uncertainty superimposed (logical, TRUE or FALSE). Default=FALSE.

genplot_extracted

Plot the data with the extracted cycle (blue) on top of it (logical, TRUE or FALSE). Default=FALSE.

keep_editable

Keep the plot settings active after the call so that extra features can be added to the plots (logical, TRUE or FALSE); FALSE restores the previous graphical parameters. Default=FALSE.

palette_name

Name of the colour palette of the power (colour) scale, a character string. Which names are valid depends on color_brewer:

  • color_brewer = "grDevices": "rainbow", "heat.colors", "terrain.colors", "topo.colors", "cm.colors", or any of the 115 hcl.colors palettes (list them with grDevices::hcl.pals()), for example "viridis", "Plasma", "Inferno", "YlOrRd", "Spectral", "Blue-Red", "Zissou 1".

  • color_brewer = "viridis": "viridis", "magma", "inferno", "plasma", "cividis", "rocket", "mako", "turbo".

  • color_brewer = "RColorBrewer": "BrBG", "PiYG", "PRGn", "PuOr", "RdBu", "RdGy", "RdYlBu", "RdYlGn", "Spectral", "Accent", "Dark2", "Paired", "Pastel1", "Pastel2", "Set1", "Set2", "Set3", "Blues", "BuGn", "BuPu", "GnBu", "Greens", "Greys", "Oranges", "OrRd", "PuBu", "PuBuGn", "PuRd", "Purples", "RdPu", "Reds", "YlGn", "YlGnBu", "YlOrBr", "YlOrRd" (also listed by wr_brewer_palettes()).

  • color_brewer = "colorRamps": "blue2green", "blue2green2red", "blue2red", "blue2yellow", "cyan2yellow", "green2red", "magenta2green", "matlab.like", "matlab.like2", "ygobb".

  • color_brewer = "scico" (all except "batlowK" need the scico package): "acton", "bam", "bamako", "bamO", "batlow", "batlowK", "batlowW", "berlin", "bilbao", "broc", "brocO", "buda", "bukavu", "cork", "corkO", "davos", "devon", "fes", "glasgow", "grayC", "hawaii", "imola", "lajolla", "lapaz", "lipari", "lisbon", "managua", "navia", "nuuk", "oleron", "oslo", "roma", "romaO", "tofino", "tokyo", "turku", "vanimo", "vik", "vikO".

Low power is drawn with the first colour of the palette and high power with the last. Default="viridis".

color_brewer

Palette family from which palette_name is taken, a character string: "grDevices", "viridis", "RColorBrewer", "colorRamps" or "scico" (the last one, except for "batlowK", needs the scico package). See palette_name for the palette names of each family. Default="viridis".

colour_brewer

British spelling of color_brewer, with the same options; if given (not NULL) it overrides color_brewer. Default=NULL.

Value

Signal extracted from the wavelet spectra. Output is a matrix with the first column being depth/time and the second column is the astronomical cycle extracted from the proxy record

If genplot_uncertainty_wt=TRUE then a wavelet spectra will be plotted with the uncertainty superimposed on top of it. In the plot the red curve and blue curves are the upper and lower bounds based on the multi parameter.The black curve is the Default=tracked_cycle_curve curve. If genplot_extracted=TRUE plot with the data set and the extracted cycle on top of it will be plotted.

References

Angi Roesch and Harald Schmidbauer (2018). WaveletComp: Computational Wavelet Analysis. R package version 1.1. https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=WaveletComp

Gouhier TC, Grinsted A, Simko V (2021). R package biwavelet: Conduct Univariate and Bivariate Wavelet Analyses. (Version 0.20.21), https://github.com/tgouhier/biwavelet

Torrence, C., and G. P. Compo. 1998. A Practical Guide to Wavelet Analysis. Bulletin of the American Meteorological Society 79:61-78. https://paos.colorado.edu/research/wavelets/bams_79_01_0061.pdf

Gabor, Dennis. "Theory of communication. Part 1: The analysis of information." Journal of the Institution of Electrical Engineers-part III: radio and communication engineering 93, no. 26 (1946): 429-441. doi:10.1049/ji-3-2.1946.0074

Russell, Brian, and Jiajun Han. "Jean Morlet and the continuous wavelet transform. " CREWES Res. Rep 28 (2016): 115. https://www.crewes.org/Documents/ResearchReports/2016/CRR201668.pdf

Morlet, Jean, Georges Arens, Eliane Fourgeau, and Dominique Glard. "Wave propagation and sampling theory—Part I: Complex signal and scattering in multilayered media. " Geophysics 47, no. 2 (1982): 203-221.

J. Morlet, G. Arens, E. Fourgeau, D. Giard; Wave propagation and sampling theory; Part II, Sampling theory and complex waves. Geophysics 1982 47 (2): 222–236.

Author

Code based on the reconstruct function of the 'WaveletComp' R package which is based on the wavelet 'MATLAB' code written by Christopher Torrence and Gibert P. Compo (1998). The assignment of the standard deviation of the uncertainty of the wavelet is based on the work of Gabor (1946) and Russell et al., (2016)

Examples

# \donttest{
#Extract the 405 kyr eccentricity cycle from the magnetic susceptibility
#record of the Sullivan core of Pas et al., (2018) and use the Gabor
# uncertainty principle to define the mathematical uncertainty of the
# analysis and use a factor of that standard deviation to define
# boundaries

# perform the CWT
mag_wt <- analyse_wavelet(data = mag,
dj = 1/100,
lowerPeriod = 0.1,
upperPeriod = 254,
verbose = FALSE,
omega_nr = 10)

#Track the 405 kyr eccentricity cycle in a wavelet spectra

#mag_track <- track_period_wavelet(astro_cycle = 405,
#                                   wavelet=mag_wt,
#                                   n.levels = 100,
#                                   periodlab = "Period (metres)",
#                                   x_lab = "depth (metres)",
#                                   palette_name="rainbow",
#                                   color_brewer="grDevices")

#Instead of tracking, the tracked solution data set mag_track_solution is used
mag_track <- mag_track_solution

mag_track_complete <- completed_series(
  wavelet = mag_wt,
  tracked_curve = mag_track,
  period_up = 1.2,
  period_down = 0.8,
  extrapolate = TRUE,
  genplot = FALSE
)

# smooth the tracking of the 405 kyr eccentricity cycle
mag_track_complete <- loess_auto(time_series = mag_track_complete,
genplot = FALSE, print_span = FALSE)

# extract the 405 kyr eccentricity cycle from the wavelet spectrum and use
# the Gabor uncertainty principle to define the mathematical uncertainty of
# the analysis and use a multiple of the derived standard deviation to define boundaries

mag_405_ecc <- extract_signal_standard_deviation(
wavelet = mag_wt,
tracked_cycle_curve = mag_track_complete,
multi = 1,
extract_cycle = 405,
tracked_cycle_period = 405,
add_mean = TRUE,
tune = FALSE,
genplot_uncertainty_wt = FALSE,
genplot_extracted = FALSE,
keep_editable=FALSE,
palette_name="rainbow",
color_brewer="grDevices"
)
# }
